about: Starter list written 15 Sep 2026 from what Dubai buyers, tenants, investors and developers routinely ask, checked against the app's screens and data that day. Naj's notes add what it missed. No personal data belongs in this file.

statuses.answered: the app answers it today; where names the screen and link

statuses.needs_data: new data would be needed; source names the likely one

links: both links = the client link and Naj's private link; private link = only with the residents key

questions.question: Is there a pharmacy nearby?
aliases: where can I buy medicine nearby
questions.note: UNBLOCKED BY A SOURCE WE ALREADY HOLD, and NOT by the licence route. The DED commerce registry is dead for this - see blockers.licence_address_is_not_premises. But g_dha__sheryan_facility_detail carries 1,760 facilities in category 'Pharmacy', of which 1,419 are status FAC_ACT and 1,212 are active AND carry a real Dubai position (207 more sit on the 90/90 placeholder). These are LICENSED PREMISES, positioned, city-wide - Dubai Marina 44, Al Barsha First 36, Warsan First 33, Jabal Ali First 31, Mirdif 26, Al Karama 26. The only reason a pharmacy is not on the map is that pharmacy is not one of the nine shipped amenity kinds; the register is already ours and already the source of the 1,562 dha clinic points. Measured 23 Sep 2026. | CORRECTED 23 Sep and again after the 24 Sep rebuild: THE USABLE COUNT IS 482, NOT 1,212. All 1,212 active positioned pharmacies carry latitude at 2 decimal places - 1,212 of 1,212, not a subset - so each sits on a north-south line and passes a range check while failing any proximity claim. _dha_precise_points.json repairs 480 of them within the 1,150 m guard, rejects 9 on the longitude test and 0 on distance, and gives a position to 7 of the 207 placeholder rows: 482 usable for 'a pharmacy 300 m away'. The other 737 still support 'there are N pharmacies in this community'. Verified here independently of the DDA session's count, same four rejections. | BUILT 24 Sep 2026, NOT YET LIVE. pharmacy is now the tenth amenity kind: PHARMACY_SUB in amenities_official.py admits the walk-in sub-categories (Community/Retail, Ambulatory, Compounding, Drug store, Clinic within Pharmacy) and EXCLUDES Hospital Pharmacy and Hospital (In Patient) Pharmacy - 46 active facilities that dispense to wards, whose presence on a map would answer a different question from the one asked. A trial build gives 1,437 items, 727 flagged approximate, clinic 1,812 and hospital 56 unchanged. LIVE 24 Sep 2026 07:21. Shipped client-first because the client half is azimuth-worker-stack 0abd26b and MUST deploy BEFORE the data, since the client indexes AMEN[i.k][2] unguarded and an unknown kind throws. VERIFIED ON THE WIRE from this session, not taken on report: /img/amenities returns 5,075 items, pharmacy 1,437 of them with 727 approximate, clinic 1,812 and hospital 56 unchanged, and ZERO pharmacies whose sub-category mentions hospital - the ward exclusion holds in the served data and not only in the builder.

questions.question: Is there a mosque nearby?
questions.source: Islamic Affairs (IACAD) mosque register, or OpenStreetMap places of worship
questions.note: NOT ANSWERABLE FROM THE COMMERCE REGISTRY AT ALL - mosques are not commercially licensed, so DED holds zero. They sit with Islamic Affairs. Needs OSM/Overture or an Islamic Affairs source. Measured 23 Sep. | 24 Sep 2026, THE ISLAMIC AFFAIRS SOURCE IS ON THE LAKE AND IT IS NOT A REGISTER. The old note said 'needs OSM/Overture or an Islamic Affairs source', which would send the next reader to look for IACAD data, find it, and lose a day. We hold g_iacad__mosque_donation: 300 rows, 206 distinct mosques, 69 areas - a DONATIONS table, so its coverage is whichever mosques received one, not Dubai's mosques. Names and locations are ARABIC ONLY (same trap as DLD project_name), location is a sub-community name with no coordinate, and 19 rows read 'NA'. The two g_stats masjid tables are aggregates - counts by broad zone (Bur Dubai, Deira, Rural) and by capacity band, by year - not individual mosques. STILL BLOCKED for a map pin, and now blocked for a reason somebody can act on: what is needed is a POSITIONED register, which OSM/Overture remains the only realistic route to.

questions.source: lk_service_charges (service_category 'Unit A/C (Charges)'), DLD service charge register
questions.note: the only cooling data held is one free-zone plant | UPGRADED TO held, 24 Sep 2026 - we hold it, no screen shows it. lk_service_charges carries a service_category of 'Unit A/C (Charges)': 1,905 rows across 209 distinct projects, budget years 2017-2023, median 5.00 AED/sqft (min 0, max 90 - the tail needs a look before any figure is quoted). So for those 209 projects we can say what cooling costs per square foot and which management company bills it. TWO LIMITS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT: (1) 209 of 694 projects have the line at all, so it is 30% coverage, and (2) THE ABSENCE OF THE LINE DOES NOT MEAN COOLING IS INCLUDED - district cooling is commonly billed direct by Empower or Emicool and never appears in a service charge schedule at all. 'No A/C line' means 'this schedule does not bill it', not 'it is free'. management_company is the service-charge manager, not necessarily the chiller provider, so it answers 'who bills it' and not 'who supplies it'.

blockers.amenity_position: Q002, Q010, Q012, Q031 are ONE blocker. The DED commerce registry identifies a licensed pharmacy, gym, petrol station or nursery but carries NO position. The chain to a parcel was proved 23 Sep: DED licence -> g_det__licence.issueauthoritylicencenumber 81.5%, unifiedlicencenumber -> det_address.id 433,675 licences, 302,135 of those carrying a parcelid. So the licence DOES reach a parcel. | 23 Sep, ON THE COMPLETE TABLE: the chain roughly doubled (DET licence -> det_address 85.8%, address carries a parcel 52.2%), and the coordinates are still NOT a position source - the table looks like it carries lat/lon on 56.9% of rows, but 1,146,316 of those pairs are exactly (0.0, 0.0) and only 27,258 rows (1.3%) hold a real Dubai position. 'Most det_address rows have coordinates' is the trap. See blockers.det_address_intersection.
blockers.parcel_is_not_a_building: A PARCEL IS NOT A BUILDING and the wording must say so. 82,856 parcels citywide hold more than one building; 301 of the 1,254 plots we draw (24%) hold more than one. SUPPORTED: 'there is a pharmacy on this plot' and 'N pharmacies within X of this plot'. NOT SUPPORTED: 'there is a pharmacy in this building' or 'the pharmacy is in the podium'. On a standalone retail plot those collapse to the same claim; on a tower-plus-podium plot they do not, and that is exactly where a buyer asks. The same grain error published a height figure of 2,341 buildings on 23 Sep whose true value was 113, because the id joined on meant 'the tallest building on the plot'.
blockers.our_ceiling_not_theirs: Measured 23 Sep, and it decides whether finishing det_address is worth fighting the gateway for: BOTH ceilings on an amenity claim are OURS, not the DDA pull's. 'On this plot' needs only a parcel key, and 1,672 of 7,155 named buildings with a record (23.4%) reach one - bounded by the footprint-to-property_id gap, not by det_address. 'Within X metres' needs a POSITION for the amenity's parcel, and we can place 1,156 of 82,440 known parcels (1.4%) - bounded by footprint bindings, which need GeoDubai or new binding work. Completing det_address lifts NEITHER until our own binding improves.
blockers.det_address_intersection: MEASURED 23 Sep 2026 against the DDA session's completed det_address (35,971 parcel ids). THE PARCELS ARE NOT NEW: 28,711 of their ids parse through keys.parcel_key, and 28,710 of those (100.0%) were already in lk_parcel_keys via dm_address_parcel. Exactly ONE key was new. What det_address adds is the link from a LICENCE to a parcel, never the parcel. THEIR LIST IS NOT NORMALISED IN OUR SENSE: 3,387 of the 35,971 strings (9.4%) our canonical parcel_key refuses - '106 - 230' (spaces round the hyphen, 1,417), '0117.645' (dot separator, 738), '0214/550' (slash, 305), '0621--0', 'TP010103', 'C-001-005'. A widened rule recovers 188 more keys and 88 genuinely new ones; it was NOT merged into keys.py, because widening the canonical key changes every join in the lake and is a decision, not a cleanup. THE TWO CEILINGS, both ours: 'on this plot' - 20,308 of their parcels reach a DLD property, but only 3,783 sit under exactly ONE dm building, so on the other 16,525 the honest sentence is 'on this plot', never 'in this tower'. 'Within X metres' - only 429 of 28,899 (1.5%) are among our 1,156 placeable plots, concentrated in Business Bay 100, Marsa Dubai 61, Al Hebiah Fourth 35, Al Thanyah Fifth 32. AND THE ROW THAT SUPPORTS BOTH AT ONCE - placeable AND single-building - IS 32 PLOTS CITY-WIDE. That is the real ceiling on 'there is a pharmacy 200 metres away, in that tower', and completing det_address did not move it. | PROVENANCE, checked 23 Sep and it changes what the 100% match means: dm_address_parcel is NOT a DM dataset. graph_load_dm.py loads it from 'the DET business-licence ADDRESS register served under data.dubai, cdn path det/open/address' - the SAME register the DDA session pulls through the iPaaS gateway. The 100% overlap is one source counted twice, not two sources agreeing, and must never be quoted as corroboration. THE ROW COUNTS ARE THE REAL FINDING: our data.dubai CSV load holds 1,050,385 address rows over 35,980 plots; their complete gateway pull holds 2,062,416 rows over 35,971 plots. DOUBLING THE ROWS PRODUCED NINE FEWER PLOTS. The plot ceiling is a property of the register, not of the pull's completeness - so finishing det_address was never the bottleneck for parcel coverage. The licence->parcel EDGE is the genuine gain. Raw string overlap, no normalisation either side: 35,970 in both, 1 only theirs ('1214'), 10 only ours - and all ten are float artefacts of our own loader ('1214.0', '381.0', '.0', '0.0'), a defect on our side, not parcels. Their letter-prefixed ids (217: TP 60, C-9-9 57, A-9-9 13, TPHQB, D9.B.9, AC9-9) all fall inside the 3,387 our canonical key refuses, so nothing is silently missed. OUR COPY CORROBORATES THE (0.0, 0.0) FINDING INDEPENDENTLY: only 6,157 of our 35,980 plots carry a position, and only 12,738 of 1,050,385 address rows carried their own - the rest backfilled from the DLD plot register. Same emptiness, two different pulls: it is the source, not the gateway. | CORRECTED 23 Sep, later the same day, and this RETIRES the row-count comparison above: the DDA session compared ids one by one and dm_address on our lake holds 2,062,416 rows - exactly their gateway count, all ids in both, zero on either side alone, same parcel on every shared id. It is one register, one copy, reached by two routes; their pull added nothing, not rows, not plots, not the licence->parcel edge, because dm_address.id plus plot_no already carried it. MY 1,050,385 WAS NOT A STALE HALF-LOAD and was not read off a header: it is sum(addresses) over dm_address_parcel, i.e. the rows that carry a USABLE PLOT ID. Rebuilding the roll-up from dm_address today returns 35,980 plots over 1,050,385 rows again - identical. So 'they doubled the rows and got nine fewer plots' was comparing a row count against a plot-bearing row count and should not be quoted. THE FACT THAT SURVIVES, and it is the better one: HALF THE REGISTER HAS NO PARCEL. Of 2,062,416 rows, 1,050,385 (50.9%) carry a usable plot id, 688,420 (33.4%) are NULL and 323,611 (15.7%) are the string '0'. A further 156,835 rows carry no emirate either, and none of those has a plot. The 52.2% 'address carries a parcel' figure from the DDA side is the same ceiling seen from the other end - it is the register's, not the pull's. | THE CANONICAL KEY WIDENED, 24 Sep 2026 (keys.py commit 469f2fb), and I re-ran the intersection rather than assuming. keys.parcel_key now reads a DOT as the community-plot separator ('0117.645' -> 1170645) and truncates a 5+ digit parcel's sub-parcel suffix ('4238153.2' -> 4238153). The dot half is strongly evidenced: read as community-plot 693 of 748 dotted strings reach a real DLD parcel, read as a number 1 does, and the SQL twin had been silently rounding '0117.645' to 118 - 203 of them onto the NEIGHBOURING community. RE-RUN RESULT: canonical parses 28,711 -> 28,766 distinct keys, refusals 3,387 -> 2,651, the 738 dot-separated strings having moved across. NO CONCLUSION MOVED - still 100% of their parcels already ours, still 20,308 reaching a DLD property, still 3,783 under exactly one building, still 32 both placeable and single-building. The only change is that 'NEW to us' went 1 -> 0: under the widened key the whole list lands inside our universe with nothing left over. Still refused, deliberately: spaces round the separator ('106 - 230', 1,417), slashes ('0214/550'), doubled hyphens, and letter prefixes (TP, C-, A-). THE SUB-PARCEL HALF WAS SPLIT BACK OUT, and this is why parent_parcel_key exists. 469f2fb briefly folded sub-parcel truncation into the canonical key: '4238153.2' produced its PARENT's key, so a join on parcel_key pulled a sub-parcel's rows in under the parent and a per-parcel count could rise without the register changing. That is a semantic change, not a spelling fix - every other rule in parcel_key maps spellings of ONE parcel onto one key, and this one mapped a DIFFERENT parcel onto its parent. SETTLED in f4a65cf: keys.parcel_key and parcel_key_sql REFUSE sub-parcels again ('4238153.2' -> None), and parent_parcel_key / parent_parcel_key_sql truncate (never round) for callers that explicitly want the parent. Nothing calls them yet. Verified here across 12 spellings, both twins agreeing. The intersection re-ran at 28,765 canonical keys, one fewer than under the folded rule, and every conclusion held: 100% already ours, 0 new, 20,308 reaching a DLD property, 3,783 under exactly one building, 429 placeable, 32 both. REBUILT AND VERIFIED 24 Sep 06:29-06:30: lk_parcel_keys now reads 28,765 distinct keys for dm_address_parcel (125,503 in total) and the stale merged key is gone. blockers.licence_address_is_not_premises: THE TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE REACHED A SCREEN. Measured by the DDA session 23 Sep 2026 and checked here: a DED/DET licence address is where a company is REGISTERED, not where it trades. On the 32 plots that are both placeable and single-building, ALL NINE 'Gas Station' licences sit in Business Bay office towers of 19 to 39 floors. A forecourt is not on the 29th floor. Plot 3460481 is a 29-floor tower carrying 2,663 active licences across 93 units - about 29 per unit - and its commonest activities are tiling, painting, carpentry and project management: contractors with a registered office, not tenants with a door. 26 of those 28 plots are towers of the same shape. THIS IS A MEANING PROBLEM, NOT A GRAIN PROBLEM. Solving footprint->property_id would not fix it; GeoDubai 2165 would not fix it; completing det_address did not fix it. The register records registration, and nothing we hold records trading premises. det_address carries addresstype and unittype, but addresstype is empty on 88% of 2,062,416 rows, both are bare codes, and DET publishes no lookup - every DET table on the lake was checked. So 'there is a pharmacy on this plot' is NOT SUPPORTED. What is supported is 'a company licensed for pharmacy is registered at an address on this plot', which is not the question a buyer asks. Some of the 38 pharmacy licences on those plots are surely real shopfronts - a podium pharmacy is ordinary - but the data cannot say which, and the petrol case shows the contamination is large, not marginal. CHECKED ON OUR SIDE, 23 Sep: NOTHING LICENCE-DERIVED HAS EVER REACHED THE APP. All 3,638 rows of data/board/amenities.json come from premises-level registers - dha 1,562, osm 966, dewa 345, dha+overture 282, khda 221, ocm 68, rta 66, ese 48, dm+google 30, dha+google 24, khda+google 17, trakhees-gap 6, dm 3. No DED and no DET. The nine kinds shipped are clinic, ev, park, supermarket, school, mall, beach, metro, hospital. Nothing to withdraw; this blocker is a fence, not a recall. | FIXED IN THE LOADER 23 Sep: scripts/graph_load_dm.py described this register as 'one row per licensed premises' in its module header, its inline comment AND in the evidence note it writes to the ledger (attribute businesses_addressed). All three now say REGISTERED address and name the gas-station case, because a header is where the next person forms their idea of what a register means. The ledger text only changes on the next graph_load_dm.py run; rows written before that still carry the old wording.
blockers.placeholder_coordinates: THREE REGISTERS, THREE DIFFERENT PLACEHOLDERS, and each one inflates an apparent coverage figure. Measured 23 Sep 2026. det_address: appears to carry lat/lon on 56.9% of 2,062,416 rows, but 1,146,316 pairs are exactly (0.0, 0.0) and only 27,258 rows (1.3%) hold a real Dubai position. g_dha__sheryan_facility_detail: the placeholder is (90, 90) - 207 of 1,419 active pharmacy facilities carry it. g_khda__ti_search: (0, 0) again. ALWAYS RANGE-CHECK A COORDINATE (lat 24.5-25.6, lon 54.5-56.5) BEFORE COUNTING IT; a null check passes all three. Also in the DHA register: xcoordinate is the LATITUDE and ycoordinate the LONGITUDE despite the names, and x arrives truncated to 2 decimal places while y is full precision - repaired for the amenity points by the 22-23 Sep commits. | IT IS ROUNDING, NOT TRUNCATION - measured 23 Sep across 1,551 accepted repairs: our latitude equals theirs FLOORED on 851 (54.9%) and ROUNDED on 700 (45.1%), ceil 0, neither 0. Floor and round coincide whenever the third decimal is below 5, so 55/45 is what rounding predicts and truncation cannot produce. THE ERROR IS +/-555 m, NOT 0 TO -1,110 m: residual median 277 m, p90 481 m, max 588 m. Halve every 'about 1.1 km' written anywhere. FIXED AT SOURCE 23 Sep: the DDA session corrected scripts/build_dha_points.py and regenerated _dha_precise_points.json, whose note now reads 'rounded to two decimals of latitude (+/-0.005 deg, about +/-555 m; measured max 588 m)' and names longitude agreement as a free second test. Positions and guard_metres 1150 unchanged, verified here: the pharmacy count is then 480 repaired / 4 rejected / 7 placeholder positioned = 487; after the 24 Sep rebuild under the aligned guard it is 475 / 9 / 7 = 482. LONGITUDE IS A FREE SHARPER TEST THE DISTANCE GUARD DOES NOT USE: only latitude lost precision, so on a genuine repair the longitudes must agree EXACTLY. All 6 rows the guard rejects have differing longitude, and 1,537 of the 1,551 it accepts agree to six decimals. 'Longitude agrees AND distance <= 700 m' would reject 20 instead of 6, catching 14 rows at 58-630 m whose longitudes differ by up to 0.0023 deg - not one point recorded twice. NOT CHANGED: tightening the guard moves facilities, so it is Kendall's call. Written up in the docstring of scripts/amenities_official.py precise_points(). | TWO COUNTS THAT LOOK LIKE A DISAGREEMENT AND ARE NOT: this session measured floor-first and got 851 floor / 700 round over 1,551 repairs; the DDA session measured round-first and got 1,026 round / 1 floor-only over 1,027. Floor and round give the same answer whenever the third decimal is below 5 - about half the time - so whichever test runs first collects the coincidences. Different populations, different ordering, same conclusion: rounding, +/-555 m. Their independently measured residual was median 276 m, p90 484 m, max 588 m against ours of 277 / 481 / 588. | THE GUARD IS THE SAME IN BOTH LANES, 24 Sep 2026, on Kendall's instruction. Two tests, not one: the longitude must agree to six decimals AND the point must move no more than 600 m. Longitude is the sharper of the two and was free all along - only latitude lost precision, so a repair that also moves the longitude describes a DIFFERENT facility rather than the same one placed better, however short the hop. The 14 rows that catches sit at 58-630 m, well inside any distance threshold anyone would have picked. 600 m rather than 1,150 because the measured maximum genuine residual is 588 m. build_district_cuts.py (828b78a) applies it to the district counts; scripts/amenities_official.py applies it to the shipped amenity set via PRECISE_GUARD_M and PRECISE_LON_EPS, which are module constants next to a note saying to change them together. _dha_precise_points.json still carries guard_metres 1150 - that is the producer's value and another session's artefact, so the amenity lane takes the tighter of the two rather than editing it. THE LANES MUST STAY IN STEP: the district count reads the raw lake table and the amenity lane writes amenities.json, so a guard that differs between them places one facility two ways and two screens disagree with no visible cause. That is how the split was found in the first place. | THE REBUILD LANDED, 24 Sep 2026, and the guard turns out to be ONE test rather than two. Both lanes rebuilt under longitude-identical AND <=600 m. Pharmacy: 1,419 active, 1,212 coarse, 475 repaired, 9 rejected on longitude, ZERO rejected on distance, 7 placeholder rows given a position = 482 usable, down from 487 under the old 1,150 m distance-only rule. The amenity set: 878 health facilities repaired, 11 rejected on longitude, ZERO on distance; 3,638 items unchanged; 10 positions moved (9 clinics, 1 hospital), median 284 m, max 631 m - 7 fell back to the coarse DHA point, 2 snapped to Overture, 1 to a cached Google answer; health 'approximate' rose 712 -> 719. THE ARITHMETIC RECONCILES EXACTLY, which is the check that matters: 480 repaired + 4 rejected = 484 candidates under the old rule, 475 + 9 = 484 under the new, so five pharmacies moved from repaired to rejected and nothing appeared or vanished. ZERO DISTANCE REJECTIONS IN EITHER LANE MEANS THE 600 m BOUND IS DOING NO WORK - every genuine repair sits inside it and every bad one is caught by the longitude test first. The distance threshold is a belt to the longitude test's braces; do not let anyone 'tune' it in the belief that it is what decides anything. If a distance rejection ever appears, that is new behaviour and worth reading, not a number to adjust. NOT DEPLOYED BY EITHER OF US: the DDA session ran the builds with --no-push and sent the deploy request to the Azimuth Rings session, which is the sole deployer. | CLOSED IN CODE, OPEN ON THE LIVE SITE, DELIBERATELY - 24 Sep 2026. The map's `amenities` layer is live with the aligned guard, pushed by Rings and verified on the wire: 3,638 items, 719 approximate, no disk-to-worker difference. The stacks' `district_amenities` still carry the OLD distance-only guard. The new district cuts exist on disk but only reach the site through a 32-district build_scheme_links run plus 32 stack pushes, and the DDA session chose not to do that to move about ten facilities - it would have collided with the bldgfacts and geo work landed since the last stack push. That is the right call: a 32-push rebuild to correct ten positions by a few hundred metres buys less than it risks. SO THE TWO LIVE LAYERS CAN DISAGREE ON AT MOST ~10 HEALTH FACILITIES, EACH WITHIN 631 m, until the next deliberate stack rebuild, which the cuts will ride along with. This is a deployment lag, not a defect: do not report it as a regression, and do not 'fix' it by pushing stacks out of band. FOR FILMING (bible 14.3): never put the map's amenity layer and the building page's LOCATION axis in the same frame until they agree on that district. A viewer cannot tell a deployment lag from an error, and on camera it reads as the app contradicting itself. No episode has done this so far.
blockers.personal_data_dha_professionals: THE FIRST PERSONAL-DATA TABLE ON THE LAKE. Published 24 Sep 2026 on Kendall's decision: the DHA professional register, 198,830 named health professionals with phone, email, gender and nationality. THE RULE: nothing on a screen, in a dossier, in a video or in a caption may NAME an individual from it, and nothing may COUNT individuals from it either - a count is a headline away from a name, and 'how many Filipino nurses work in this tower' is a question this register can answer and we will not. Any use beyond the one below is a deliberate decision by Kendall, recorded before it ships, not a judgement made while building. THE ONE SANCTIONED USE, and it touches no person: the register keeps FACILITY positions at full precision, which is what _dha_precise_points.json extracts to repair the facility register's rounded latitudes (see blockers.placeholder_coordinates). That is a building's position, not a practitioner's, and it stays. Do not read this blocker as 'do not use the table' and revert the 482 pharmacy repairs; read it as 'the people in it are not ours to show'. Nothing shipped draws on it today: all 3,638 rows of data/board/amenities.json come from facility-level and premises-level sources, checked 23 Sep - see blockers.licence_address_is_not_premises.

blockers.ridership_is_taps_not_journeys: METRO AND TRAM RE-DERIVED 24 Sep 2026 on the republished tables, after the first publish was doubled (the portal writes each part as CSV and again as JSON; the loader summed both, and the exact-row check compared against that same sum, so it confirmed the doubling - and so did my own first check). pp_rta__metro_ridership 22,017,813 rows: Check in 11,117,461, Check out 10,900,352. pp_rta__tram_ridership 21,012,968 rows: Check in 11,014,186, Check out 9,998,782. THREE THINGS BEFORE ANY FIGURE IS QUOTED. (1) IT IS AN EXTRACT, NOT A CENSUS. Metro runs about 1-3 million taps a year here, roughly two orders of magnitude below RTA's published annual metro ridership. (2) 12,283,618 of the metro rows carry no time at all (txn_time 00:00:00.000), so hour-of-day analysis covers only the remaining ~9.7M, and exact-duplicate counts on metro are mostly untimed rows colliding naturally - timed duplicates decay smoothly (1,143,450 pairs, 235,019 triples, 44,549 fours), which is people tapping together, not a copied part. (3) TRAM STILL HAS A REPEATED BLOCK AND A GAP.
